# 003 · Logging a timestamp makes the decision unverifiable

[← All examples](../README.md)

| Verdict | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change | Verified unit | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **⚠ Unverifiable** | determinism | medium | logging, behaviour change not intended | [`OrderLifecycle#decide`](../../apps/boxoffice/ticketing-domain/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/boxoffice/ticketing/domain/OrderLifecycle.java) | [B8: Behavioural contracts](../../tools/contracts/README.md) |

> Appending the current time to a reason string looks like harmless diagnostics. It makes the state machine depend on the clock, so its behaviour can no longer be proved, and the verifier refuses.

## The change

Add when a decision was made to the 'unchanged' reason, to help debug redelivered events.

**Before** ([`OrderLifecycle.java`](../../apps/boxoffice/ticketing-domain/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/boxoffice/ticketing/domain/OrderLifecycle.java), line 62):

```java
    private static Decision transition(OrderStatus next, Effect... effects) {
        return new Decision.Transition(next, List.of(effects));
    }

    private static Decision unchanged(String reason) {
        return new Decision.Unchanged(reason);
    }
}
```

**After:**

```java
    private static Decision transition(OrderStatus next, Effect... effects) {
        return new Decision.Transition(next, List.of(effects));
    }

    private static Decision unchanged(String reason) {
        return new Decision.Unchanged(reason + " (checked at " + java.time.Instant.now() + ")");
    }
}
```

<details><summary>Patch</summary>

```diff
--- a/apps/boxoffice/ticketing-domain/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/boxoffice/ticketing/domain/OrderLifecycle.java
+++ b/apps/boxoffice/ticketing-domain/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/boxoffice/ticketing/domain/OrderLifecycle.java
@@ -62,8 +62,8 @@
     private static Decision transition(OrderStatus next, Effect... effects) {
         return new Decision.Transition(next, List.of(effects));
     }
 
     private static Decision unchanged(String reason) {
-        return new Decision.Unchanged(reason);
+        return new Decision.Unchanged(reason + " (checked at " + java.time.Instant.now() + ")");
     }
 }
```

</details>

## What the verifier found

The verifier refused to produce a verdict, because the method is no longer provably pure:

- `net.terminalvalue.boxoffice.ticketing.domain.OrderLifecycle.unchanged calls java.time.Instant.now, which is not known to be pure`

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

No: every existing unit test passes (`:ticketing-domain:test`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

The order state machine is meant to be a pure function: the same status and input must always give the same decision. That is what makes redelivered Kafka events safe to replay, and what lets the decision be tested exhaustively. With a clock read inside, two replicas or two deliveries of the same event produce different results, and any equality check on decisions becomes flaky.

## Why the verdict is right

Before running anything, the verifier walks the bytecode of every method decide can reach. It finds a call from OrderLifecycle.unchanged to java.time.Instant.now, which is not on the list of JDK APIs trusted to be pure. Without purity, running every input proves nothing, so the verifier refuses instead of producing a contract.

## What to do

Log the timestamp in the adapter that applies the decision (OrderTransitions), outside the pure core. If the time really matters to the decision, pass it in as a parameter, which makes it part of the contract's input domain.
